# Tables, ready to paste

**Generated by `docs/article/make_tables.py`. Do not edit by hand** —
regenerate it, so a number here cannot drift from the run it came from.

Source: `benchmarks/results/2026-08-27/`, commit
`e8a2065`, corpus digest `cd2d48ccf99bddb4`,
Linux 6.18.44-fc-v22 on x86_64, Python 3.11.15,
4 cores, N=5.

> **Every count in this file is UTF-8 bytes, not model tokens.** The
> environment these were measured in cannot reach a tokenizer vocabulary.
> A byte figure is a lower bound on cost, an upper bound on saving, and
> not a reliable ordering — on this project's own tabular data the two
> units disagreed by 24 points and did not rank five serialisation
> formats in the same order. If you quote these as token savings you are
> saying something we did not measure.

Fidelity is written `score (components)`. A 1.000 from one component
and a 1.000 from four are different claims.

## Table 4 — What running a converter out of process costs

`Added RSS` is the peak resident set of this process **and its
descendants** during the cell, minus a reading taken immediately before
it. Sampled every 5 ms, so it is a lower bound.

| Backend | Runs as | Added RSS across its cells |
|---|---|---|
| `pandoc` | a separate program | 28, 64, 108, 111, 123, 124, 125 MiB |
| `libreoffice` | a separate program | 263 MiB |
| `repomix` | `npx` &rarr; `node` | 279 MiB |
| `pymupdf4llm` | a separate Python interpreter (AGPL, never imported) | 280, 282, 322 MiB |
| `kreuzberg` | in-process Python | 0 MiB |
| `trafilatura` | in-process Python | 0 MiB |

No before-count: nobody hands a model the raw bytes of a directory, so
there is nothing to subtract from. The honest figure is what the pack
costs.

## Table 6 — When converting costs more than it saves

Input that is already Markdown. There is nothing to strip, so the only
thing a converter can do is change the syntax — and one of them makes it
**larger**. This is the least flattering cell in the corpus and it is
here for that reason.

| Input | Backend | Before | After | Change | Fidelity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `structured.md` | `plaintext` | 1,469 | 1,466 | −0.2% | 1.000 (4) |
| `structured.md` | `pandoc` | 1,469 | 1,609 | +9.5% | 0.977 (4) |
| `long_context.md` | `plaintext` | 79,255 | 79,255 | −0.0% | n/a |
| `long_context.md` | `pandoc` | 79,255 | 79,255 | −0.0% | n/a |

`pandoc` re-emits `structured.md` **9.5% larger** at a slightly lower
fidelity: it normalises the Markdown into its own dialect, which is
more verbose than what was there. `plaintext` passes it through and
saves 0.2% — three bytes of trailing whitespace.

`long_context.md` is unchanged by both, to the byte. A conversion
pipeline that reports a saving on input it did not change would be
broken, and this row is what proves it is not.
